episode_title: Getting into the Energy Industry, Feat Uzoma Godspower.

real_qa.q: How did Uzoma Godspower transition from wanting to study medicine and aeronautical engineering to eventually pursuing geosciences?
real_qa.r: Uzoma initially wanted to study medicine due to his mother's preference, but abandoned this goal in secondary school after being expelled for a stone-throwing incident that made him realize he could not handle blood. He then pursued aeronautical engineering but learned only one Nigerian university (Ahmadu Bello University Zaria) offered it with limited practical training. He compromised by choosing mechanical engineering at FUTO but did not meet the cut-off; he then selected geology from the supplementary list after researching it and discovering it was related to petroleum engineering, eventually loving the geological concepts from year two onwards.
real_qa.requete: Uzoma Godspower geosciences career transition journey

real_qa.q: What role did joining the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Exploration (NAPI) play in Uzoma Godspower's entry into the energy industry?
real_qa.r: Uzoma discovered NAPI during his second year at university around 2018-2019 and began attending their monthly technical meetings online via Zoom from FUTO. This was a formative decision that expanded his knowledge base, exposed him to industry practices and professionals before he had studied them theoretically in class, and helped him build a network of mentors who provided crucial insights about the energy industry and his future prospects.
real_qa.requete: NAPI Nigerian Association Petroleum Exploration industry entry

real_qa.q: What percentage of geoscience students in Nigeria do not initially choose geosciences as their first career preference?
real_qa.r: According to Uzoma Godspower, approximately 70 to 80 percent of geoscience students in Nigeria did not choose geosciences from the onset, a category into which he himself falls. This suggests that many students in the field arrived at their discipline through circumstance or supplementary admission rather than deliberate initial choice.
real_qa.requete: geoscience students Nigeria percentage initial choice

real_qa.q: What workforce gap did Uzoma Godspower identify in the Nigerian geoscience sector between 2022 and 2023?
real_qa.r: Uzoma observed that most geoscience professionals in major Nigerian companies like Shell, Total and others were senior professionals in their 40s and 50s, with very few professionals in their early-to-mid 20s. He predicted that as these senior professionals approached retirement around 2023 onwards, companies would need to launch significant recruitment exercises to train the next generation of geoscientists to fill the impending gap, which is why he started seeing a recruitment boom in 2023.
real_qa.requete: Nigeria geoscience workforce gap retirement recruitment 2023

real_qa.q: How did Uzoma Godspower use LinkedIn and in-person NAPI conferences to build his professional network in the energy industry?
real_qa.r: Uzoma began connecting with geoscience professionals on LinkedIn while still in school, as the platform was just gaining traction in Nigeria at that time. He then attended the annual NAPI conferences held in November at a conference venue, where he would identify and meet physically with professionals he had already connected with online, moving their relationships from digital to offline and establishing credibility by putting a face to their online connection.
real_qa.requete: LinkedIn NAPI conference networking energy industry strategy

guest.bio_context: Uzoma Godspower is a geoscientist with a background in geophysics who transitioned from a business development executive role at Andana International Integrated Nigeria Limited to pursuing a career in digital science. He began his energy industry journey by joining Gigi Connect Nigeria Limited as an NYSE Copper for one year, was retained for an additional six months, and subsequently joined CEPLAT as a graduate intern in 2024.
